steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add potatoes and cook until tender but still firm, about 15 minutes. Drain and allow to cool.
Slice cooled potatoes and layer in a large bowl or dish.
In a saucepan combine water, vinegar and sugar. Bring to a boil and cook for one minute. Remove from heat and pour over potatoes. Cover and chill for at least 12 hours.
Drain excess marinade and add onions, salt, pepper, celery seed and mayonnaise. Mix well and serve chilled.

raw_recipe.headline: Bud's Potato Salad
raw_recipe.description: In this yummy salad, sliced and cooled potatoes are doused with a vinegar, sugar, and water bath and chilled for twelve hours. At the last moment, mayonnaise, celery seeds, and diced onion are folded in.
raw_recipe.name: Bud's Potato Salad

review.reviewBody:
I have made this salad 3 times now and everyone loves it.
I did make a change however. The first time I made this, I found out that I had no celery seed ( I could have sworn I did!) so I subbed dill weed for it and it's wonderful.
I also don't drain all the vinegar mixture as it gives the finished product a kick.
You will not be sorry with this recipe.

This is an excellent recipe for someone who likes the New York deli style potato salad of yore. I have made it several times, as is and with minor changes; such as using a little dill juice from the pickle jar, a little less sugar. The best time saver I have found is to buy a couple of boxes of store brand scallopped potatoes on sale, put the sauce envelope in the pantry and using only the dehydrated potatoes..boil them for about 15-16 min, then drain and put in bowl, pour marinade over the potatoes as per recipe. Proceed with recipe and is best made the day before using. Thanks, Bud.

Potato salad lovers...GO with this one! Excellent with no leftovers on a boat party! Minor changes personal taste. Scaled it back to half recipe, using one 5lb bag RED potatoes, scrub, leave peels on (easy!) cubed to about 3/4" size, simmered in tall large skillet salted water until firm (not mushy!)about 12-15 minutes. Marinated overnight in ziplock bag. Used 1 small bunch green onions (only 1/2 green parts) & some red onion. I had to add eggs (5) & celery for crunch! Do NOT be afraid to marinate the potatoes...this is what makes this recipe so special! Maybe some posters did not drain the marinade off when they posted it was mushy or vinegary??? Just a thought...

1.28.21 The single thing that makes this potato salad unique is the marinade, and it works! I think the dressing on its own is weak, so I did add some chopped hard boiled egg and crumbled bacon (gotta have bacon in my potato salad!). The potatoes need to be really WELL DRAINED, otherwise, their wetness will result in runny dressing (mine was a but). The potato marinade was a new method for me, and I enjoyed its tanginess but will cut back a little on the sugar in the future. I will use the marinade again, but use my own potato salad dressing. But bottom line, different and good.

The marinade really sets this one apart. I took other reviewers' advice and use about half the mayo. For me, potato salad MUST have hard-boiled eggs and celery, so I add about 4-6 eggs and about a cup of celery (in addition to the celery seed). I also marinade the onions along with the potatoes. This doesn't last long at my house!

My new favorite way to make potato salad! I took this to a family gathering last month, and not one bite was left! 
Due to a time constraint, I only marinated the russet potatoes for 4 hours - it was enough - and then followed the guidelines for the dressing, although I added chopped eggs, only 1 onion and fresh celery (finely chopped). Absolutely delicious! The key is in the marinade! Thanks, Diana_Leslie for sharing your Dad's recipe!

Excellent recipe! I was looking for a potato salad similar to what you'd find in a deli, and this fit the bill perfectly! I scaled it down to 5 servings because that's all I needed. I didn't discard the marinade. I tossed the potatoes around a few times, and they absorbed it. Also, some reviewers mentioned it was too sweet, so I cut back on the sugar a little, and it was still sweet enough for me. It is the sweetness though, that makes it different (in a good way) from standard potato salads. I also added some finely chopped celery and a chopped, hard-boiled egg. I was short on mayo, so I added plain Greek yogurt to compensate. Thanks DIANA_LESLIE for sharing your Dad's recipe! It's a keeper! And...GO PATS!!!!
I made this yesterday and for those cooks that think it was too sweet, try using a white onion not a sweet onion and grating the onion in a food processor....very good!

Excellent!!! I think marinating the potatoes is key to the recipe. I used red potatoes and added 5 hard boiled eggs, a jar of pickles (shredded), and a tsp of dijon mustard in addition to the basic recipe. Thank you for sharing!

I am a picky potato salad person so I'm giving this 4 stars...I've yet to have a 5 star (perfect) potato salad. I followed this recipe exactly and the day after it sat in the vinegar, we did as it said, drained the vinegar mixture and added the mayo, onion, etc. My husband and I thought it was okay but we could still really taste the vinegar. The taste was OKAY. Then, we let it sit another day with the mayo and it was DELICIOUS the next day. I would therefore make this 48 hours prior to serving...the day before with the vinegar mixture, drain, then add all the rest of the ingredients to it and allow it to sit another day. It is definitely worth the time if you have it! I would say this is definitely one of the best recipes so far!
Added mustard..what ever one u like..i change from yellow mustard ,or honey mustard or what ever goes with BBQ MEAT..GREAT
Hands down, the best potato salad EVER!!!!!

I'm a mid-west girl so I grew up eating the mayo/mustard/egg potato salad but came looking for something different. I did not care for this. The vinegar gave it way too much tang. For other mid-westerners this taste more like a warm German potato salad only it has mayo in it.

This was simply not up to par. The flavors were bland even though I took the advice of other reviewers to leave the potatoes in the marinade. And to take the potatoes out before they get soft is a HUGE mistake.
It was good, but just a tad too sweet for me.

I found this recipe on this site ages ago! I've been making it ever since. Every time I make it, it just disappears. It is one of my most requested things to bring to any BBQ or get together!! I often do not use chopped onion, but will sub with onion powder. The celery seed makes all the difference and using the white wine vinegar gives it a better flavor than just white vinegar. I will continue to make this and pass it down to my daughters!
I loved this, and so did everyone at the party! I have passed it on to several people and plan to make this a staple. My Mom is from NY and says this is as close to the NY style she's ever had in PA!

I've made this potato salad a few times now to to take to gatherings, and my friends keep asking me to make it. In addition to the celery seed, I added fresh dill, and instead of all mayonnaise, I used half mayo and half sour cream. Best potato salad EVER. No joke.
Picnic time -- everyone wanted recipe and you had to be fast to get seconds

I only use the marinade part of this recipe. It is however,The Secret to consistantly awesome potato salad. Start with the marinade process, then choose your add ins according to your families taste, then finish off with Mayo. No need to fiddle with vinegar, mustard or sugar trying to get your potato salad dressing perfectly seasoned. The marinade did all that work for!!!! Thank you Bud, I'll never make potato salad any other way!!!
